correctness.rationale: For whole-line Brownian motion generator D∂xx with transparent inactive point gate, symmetric gamma, Poisson position resets r to x0>0 leaving gate state unchanged, conditioned on incoming side at active absorption: first-zero Laplace modes a=sqrt(r/D), b=sqrt((r+2gamma)/D); no-reset inactive-origin ODE yields (b-a)/(b+a). Keeping the two gate states in renewal matrix R=r(rI-Q)^(-1) gives F_A=(1-z)(1-exp(-bx0))/4, F_I=F_A+exp(-bx0)/(2(1+z)); their stationary mean is P_-=[1-z+z²exp(-bx0)/(1+z)]/4, z=a/b. Algebraic derivatives give decrease with r and x0 and increase with gamma, with 0<P<1/4; as r,gamma->0 at r/gamma->c, P->1/[4(1+sqrt(c/(c+2)))]. Independently solved the six-condition left/right backward boundary-value system (not just copied renewal), matching exact expression to ~5e-16 at four separated parameter tuples. Principal qualifier: the closest published study states a simulation trend for initial-side capture vs gamma opposite to this analytic result; its discrete-time crossing procedure and pathwise definition must be reconciled. Independent continuum BVP and derivation support the mathematical claim, not unqualified numerical agreement with that publication.

originality.rationale: Same-model Żbik–Dybiec–Capała–Palmowski–Sokolov paper develops total first-passage transforms and simulates incoming-side fractions in Section III.3 Figure5, but supplies no analytical closed form, exact conditional probabilities or joint weak-rate crossover. However its simulation description claims increasing gamma makes initial-side probability grow, in conflict with present opposite-side formula; this is retained as a substantive comparison risk rather than called confirming evidence. Other cited gating models use reflecting inactive targets or gate-redraw resets, where opposite-side mark is absent. Best-of-knowledge original analytic split result with unresolved prior-model discrepancy, not a claim of established numerical concordance.
